races.title: State Assembly, District 45
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: James C. Ramos
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly, first elected in 2018 and now representing District 45. He is the first California Native American to serve in the Assembly. Previously a San Bernardino County supervisor and board chair, and a former chairman of the San Manuel Band of Mission Indians.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists 2026 endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Young Democrats, and Planned Parenthood of Orange and San Bernardino Counties' Community Action Fund.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2024 or 2026. The list of bills he sponsored did not display on the page we read. We found no controversies and no foreign ties. His exact birth date and the date he became tribal chairman were not found.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says he was born on and lives on the San Manuel Indian Reservation in San Bernardino County, and his campaign site calls him a lifelong resident who attended local public schools there.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2018. Before that he was elected to the San Bernardino County Board of Supervisors and served as its chair, and he was chairman of the San Manuel Band of Mission Indians. He holds a B.S. in accounting and an MBA, and was appointed to the State Board of Education and the Native American Heritage Commission.
qual.why: He has several terms of prior legislative service and held local elected office, including board chair. His accounting and MBA training fits the budget side of the job. Committee seats and appointed boards were not counted.
qual.label: He has several terms of prior legislative service and held local elected office, including board chair. His accounting and MBA training fits the budget side of the job. Committee seats and appointed boards were not counted.

cands.name: Greg Abdouch
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California Assembly District 45 in 2026. Self-described small business owner with 30+ years in sales, contract management and entrepreneurship, including 16 years running a construction business. Founded the parent group Not On Our Watch. No elected office held.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists endorsements from the Republican Party of California and Reform California, plus several voter guides: April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: His birthplace and the year he moved to or settled in California are not given. His website says both "lifelong resident" and "over 45 years" in San Bernardino County. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so there are no detailed policy answers. We found no stated positions on data centers, development and growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and teacher pay. His site speaks of parents' rights and school transparency rather than school choice. He has held no office, so there are no official actions to report. His claim to have worked alongside legislators is not specific or documented, and we could not check details of Not On Our Watch or his business career beyond his own account. No independent news coverage was available.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he was raised in Apple Valley and has called San Bernardino County home for over 45 years, but it does not give his birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: By his own account, he has 30+ years in sales, contract management and entrepreneurship, including 16 years operating a construction business, and he founded the parent advocacy group Not On Our Watch. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: Business ownership and management place him in the middle band; he has no legislative, policy or budget career or elected office. All of this comes from his campaign site and could not be independently verified.
